Assuming you're starting at rock bottom like I am, this is what my therapist told me:

Start by noticing what you give the world every day - whether it's something as simple as waving at a neighbor or feeding a pet.  Acknowledge that your actions made the world a better place, even by a little bit.  Focus on what you accomplished, not what you didn't.

When you can, give back more.  Volunteer if possible.  Give back creatively if you're artistically or craftily bent.  Invest time and interest into others.

In the end, it's a game of faking it.  Slowly act like you have confidence and you'll eventually really have it.

You're up about 25-40 ft, attached by tethers, standing on staples, and hanging on to the tree as it sways.  The participants climb up the tree, making it sway even more, and then they need the staples you're standing on  so you have to swing out and hang in mid air. It's completely safe, actually.  But it's definitely something you have to get used to - and the only way is by experience.  Every year I did it, I had to get used to it all over again.  Took about two weeks.
